provenance: M39's negative half, and the reason the retry is bounded at one. `stub_judge` repeats its LAST verdict entry forever, so `["malformed"]` is a judge that can never be read: an unbounded or backoff-looping retry would spin here (or, worse, keep spending until the token budget tripped and reported the wrong failure class), and a retry that swallowed the second failure would leave a run certified by nothing at all. The committed behaviour is ADR-017's, unchanged: `status: failure:semantic`, `verdict: FAIL`, `checks.judge_available: false` (the judge never ANSWERED -- distinct from `judge_responsive: false`, which is a judge that answered and rejected), and the existing `judge unavailable, failing closed: JudgeError: ...` reason. `judge_attempts: 2` is the only thing that differs from the pre-M39 tree, and it is what makes the bound auditable after the fact: a run that failed closed says how many times it tried. WATCHED RED FIRST -- on the pre-M39 tree `"malformed"` was not a stub verdict the harness knew, and once it was, the un-retried tree recorded no `judge_attempts` at all.

triage.note: pins that ADR-023 narrows WHEN fail-closed fires, never WHETHER it does. Paired with `judge-fail-closed-on-error` (a non-retryable JudgeError, one attempt) so the two directions of the same guard are both graded.
